chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ya'qub al-Katib, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the charity of wealth that has not yet been collected and has not yet been distributed. He said, 'It is permissible.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to give charity from wealth that has not yet been collected or distributed?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the reliable chain of Abu Basir, establishes that the validity of sadaqah depends on the owner's right of disposal rather than physical possession. In Shia fiqh, this clarifies that wealth in the hands of a trustee or awaiting division retains its status as the owner's property, allowing for charitable donation prior to actual transfer. This ruling facilitates early charitable acts and resolves disputes regarding the status of undistributed assets.
